content:
incident-bot: PagerDuty INC-2026-984 fired for gpu-pool-3 (us-west). Symptom: repeated CUDA alloc failures -> cascading OOMs, KV cache thrash. Auto-evacuation triggered but some pods failing to drain. Severity: P1. @jamal please ack and investigate.

pagerduty: Incident INC-2026-984 acknowledged by jamal at 1767543225. Escalating in 8m if not resolved.

jamal: Ack. Looking. Quick snapshot: multiple jobs (embeddings-batch) spiking allocation to ~16GB/chunk and triggering `cudaMalloc` failures. I’m going to pause the heavy batch queue and start a targeted pool drain.

maria: @jamal fyi I just saw elevated 5xx and elevated tail latency on embeddings-api from synthetic tests. Customer Success flagged two customers seeing delayed batches.

jamal: Copy. Pausing queue now: `infra-runner run jobctl pause queue embeddings-batch --reason "alloc failures"`

infra-runner: Command accepted. Paused queue embeddings-batch. Current running jobs: 12.

jamal: Dumping recent node logs (shortened):
```
[GPU_07] 2026-02-10T12:00:21Z ERROR cuda: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[GPU_07] 2026-02-10T12:00:22Z WARN kvcache: eviction storm, reclaiming 2.1GB
[GPU_12] 2026-02-10T12:00:23Z ERROR cublas: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED
[Driver] 2026-02-10T12:00:24Z INFO auto-shedder: started eviction run on pool gpu-pool-3
```

sophie: Any chance this is fragmentation rather than total mem? I remember pool-3 has mixed model sizes and older pinned kernels.

jamal: Good call. Running `nvidia-smi topo -m` and `pools describe gpu-pool-3 --show-alloc-map`. If it's fragmentation, we should drain lowest-priority pods first and restart nodes to defragment.

infra-runner: Alloc map shows many small allocations pinned across 4 gpus, combined ephemeral KV cache ~6GB, resident models ~10GB. Fragmentation index high (0.68).

jamal: Ok that's fragmentation + transient burst from embeddings-batch. Plan: 1) Pause batch (done). 2) Drain 2 lowest-util nodes in pool-3 and reboot them to clear fragmentation. 3) Reroute new requests to pool-4 (us-east) for latency-insensitive traffic. 4) If OOMs persist, scale up with a buffer node.

maria: Customer-impact note: two enterprise customers (AcmeHealth, LedgerOps) reported 10-15min job delays; no data loss, just retries/backpressure. CS is preparing comms.

jamal: Starting drain: `pools drain-node gpu-pool-3 node-1184 --grace-period 60s`

pagerduty: Reminder: If unresolved after 6m, escalate to SRE lead.

oncall-next: @jamal I’m ready to pick up once you hand off. Keep me posted on node reboots.

jamal: Node-1184 drained successfully, rebooting now (`nodectl reboot node-1184`). Kernel logs show `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` on driver attach for some pods; they restarted and freed memory. Reboot complete.

infra-runner: Node-1188 drain started. Detected one stuck pod (embedding-worker-7) that failed to terminate; force-killed it.

jamal: After one reboot, allocation failures dropped by ~70%. Monitoring: error spike is decaying. Rerouting latency-insensitive requests: `routing apply --pool gpu-pool-3 --fallback pool-4 --selector embeddings`

sophie: Nice. Are we confident this is mitigated vs just rate-limited? Any lingering leak?

jamal: Still watching. Heap of logs show KV cache reclaiming frequently but no monotonic growth in resident size over 10m. Looks like fragmentation + bursty workloads. I’ll keep batch paused for another 10m and then resume at rate-limit.

customer-success: CS update: notified AcmeHealth + LedgerOps of mitigation and they are satisfied with ETA update. No escalations to account teams.

pagerduty: INC-2026-984 updated: Mitigation in progress, monitoring.

jamal: Resuming embeddings-batch at throttled rate: `jobctl resume queue embeddings-batch --rate 0.2` (20% of normal throughput). Will keep an eye.

infra-runner: Resumption accepted; initial wave of 3 jobs scheduled.

jamal: Observed a smaller spike but no new cudaMalloc failures after throttle. I'll leave the two rebooted nodes in rotation and schedule a maintenance window to drain and reboot remaining nodes in pool-3 during low traffic (tonight).

sophie: Suggest follow-up actions: 1) add fragmentation monitor alert to detect high fragmentation-index and trigger controlled drains; 2) tune auto-shedder threshold so it triggers earlier for mixed-size pools; 3) add model pinning review for embedding workers.

jamal: Agreed. I'll open a follow-up ticket with remediation items. For now switching to handoff: @oncall-next you take post-incident watch at 1767543500; I'll stay available for 30m.

oncall-next: Taking watch. Please add any notes to the incident doc.

jamal: Short summary for incident doc: Root cause - allocation fragmentation combined with sudden embeddings-batch burst; symptom - cudaMalloc OOMs, KV cache thrash; impact - delayed batch jobs for two enterprise customers (10-15m), increased 5xx on embeddings-api; mitigation - paused batch, drained/rebooted two nodes, rerouted traffic, resumed at throttled rate; follow-ups - fragmentation alerting, auto-shedder tuning, maintenance to drain rest of pool.

customer-success: Marking customers informed. Thanks for fast response team. :heart: :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-984 status: monitoring. If stable for 30m, will auto-resolve.

jamal: Leaving a runbook note: `if fragmentation-index > 0.6 and >5 cudaMalloc failures/min -> pause batch, drain one node, reboot, reroute to fallback pool, scale buffer +1`. Adding to runbook now.

oncall-next: Acknowledged. I'll keep an eye and update if anything changes.

pagerduty: INC-2026-984 resolved automatically at 1767543775 (stable for 30m).

jamal: Closing thread. Follow-up ticket: INFRA-7421 - "gpu-pool-3 fragmentation mitigation and alerting" assigned to infra team.

sophie: Thanks all. Great run.
